messages:
Mina: dropping a new tiny-legend exploration for compact monitoring tiles. core idea: keep a single-line legend with color chip, 3-char label, and a micro-unit pill. hover or focus expands an inline flyout with full label, unit variants, smoothing indicator, and a 40px sparkline. Arlo: liking the single-line density. question: if we abbreviate labels to 3 chars how do we avoid collisions? e.g., RTT vs RTO. maybe allow smart truncation and show full name in flyout. Bea: accessibility: condensed legend must still expose full semantics to screen readers. add aria-label on the list item with full phrase: "Round-trip time p95, 12.3 ms, smoothed (5m)". flyout should be reachable via keyboard (Enter/Space) and dismiss on Escape. Tom: outlier UX: default to percentile clipping at 99.5, but show a faint dotted cap on the y-axis and a small badge on legend: "^" when clips exist. clicking ^ opens flyout with raw max and an option "show raw spikes" which overlays raw points temporarily. implement overlay as separate canvas layer to avoid reflow. Mina: microcopy samples for flyout header: - "Round-trip time (p95)" - "RTT — p95" Which is clearer inline? Arlo: prefer full name in header, short form in compact. also include a contextual link "How smoothing works" in the flyout. Bea: keyboard/ARIA sketch: ```html
  • ▣ ms
    • ``` Ensure the button toggles aria-expanded and focuses the flyout content. Tom: perf notes: compute clip flags server-side in the query so UI can render badges without extra round trips. stable keys: series_id used for DOM keys. avoid updating chart canvas when toggling flyout. ux-bot: preview available at https://staging.redwood.run/pr/3899 branch `legend/tiny-flyout`; visual snapshots for collapsed, expanded, and clipped states. Mina: action items: 1) Bea add ARIA examples and add screen reader acceptance tests; 2) Arlo propose truncation rules and collision handling; 3) Tom add server-side clip flag plan and overlay sketch. I'll update the prototype with the ^ clip badge and tiny sparkline later today. :sparkles:
